newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS backs off from EU-Virgin fight.
newsitem.headline: SAS backs off from EU-Virgin fight.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Tuesday it trimmed all its Copenhagen-Brussels fares, after complaints by Virgin Express of selective cuts.
"We have levelled prices on all our Brussels flight departures," SAS spokesman Troels Rasmussen told Reuters.
Virgin wrote to European Union transport officials in September complaining that its new budget-fare daily service from Copenhagen to Brussels was the victim of foul play by SAS.
It said that SAS cut the price of its own flights in a similar time slot but left fares on other departures for the Belgian capital unchanged.
Virgin's British owner Richard Branson at the time notified EU authorities of the situation and threatened formal action if the problem was not resolved.

"We never got any formal complaint from Branson, who only brought our attention to the problem in an informal letter," EU Transport Commission spokeswoman Sarah Lambert told the Danish financial daily Borsen on Tuesday.
"SAS then altered its pricing structure, so the problem disappeared of its own accord," she said. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
